arxiv-2109-01073.title: λ \lambda -Navier-Stokes turbulence
arxiv-2109-01073.creator: A. Alexakis 1 and L. Biferale 2
arxiv-2109-01073.description: Abstract We investigate numerically the model proposed in [ 1 ] where a parameter λ \lambda is introduced in the Navier-Stokes equations such that the weight of homochiral to heterochiral interactions is varied while preserving all original scaling symmetries and inviscid invariants.

arxiv-2210-02529.title: Factorization at subleading power in deep inelastic scattering in the x → 1 x\rightarrow 1 limit
arxiv-2210-02529.creator: Michael Luke, Jyotirmoy Roy, Aris Spourdalakis
arxiv-2210-02529.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Michael Luke, Jyotirmoy Roy, Aris Spourdalakis. We examine the endpoint region of inclusive deep inelastic scattering at next-to-leading power (NLP). Using a soft-collinear effective theory approach with no explicit soft or collinear modes, we discuss the factorization of the cross section at NLP and show that the overlap subtraction procedure introduced to eliminate double counting of degrees of freedom at leading power ensures that spurious endpoint divergences in the rate cancel at NLP at one loop.

arxiv-2401-01986.title: Generation of complete graph states in a spin- 1 / 2 1/2 Heisenberg chain with a globally optimized magnetic field
arxiv-2401-01986.creator: X. X. Li, D. X. Li, X. Q. Shao
arxiv-2401-01986.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by X. X. Li, D. X. Li, X. Q. Shao. Graph states possess significant practical value in measurement-based quantum computation, with complete graph states that exhibit exceptional performance in quantum metrology. In this work, we introduce a method for generating multiparticle complete graph states using a spin- 1 / 2 1/2 Heisenberg X ​ X XX chain subjected to a time-varying magnetic field, which applies to a wide range of systems.

arxiv-2504-14438.title: Information Diffusion and Preferential Attachment in a Network of Large Language Models
arxiv-2504-14438.creator: Adit Jain, Student Member, IEEE, Vikram Krishnamurthy, Fellow, IEEE, Yiming Zhang
arxiv-2504-14438.description: Abstract This paper models information diffusion in a network of Large Language Models (LLMs) that is designed to answer queries from distributed datasets, where the LLMs can hallucinate the answer. We introduce a two-time-scale dynamical model for the centrally administered network, where opinions evolve faster while the network’s degree distribution changes more slowly.

arxiv-2506-09254.title: Machine learning-based correlation analysis of decadal cyclone intensity with sea surface temperature: data and tutorial
arxiv-2506-09254.creator: Jingyang Wu, Rohitash Chandra
arxiv-2506-09254.description: Abstract The rising number of extreme climate events in the past decades has motivated the need for a thorough consideration of tropical cyclone genesis and intensity, given the sea-surface temperature (SST). In this paper, we present an analysis of the relationship between the increasing global SST with cyclone genesis using linear regression machine learning models.

arxiv-2602-10130.title: Fiscal Dynamics in Japan under Demographic Pressure
arxiv-2602-10130.creator: Goshi Aoki
arxiv-2602-10130.description: Abstract Japan faces a demographic transformation–a shrinking total population, a declining working-age share, and rapid elderly growth. These trends squeeze public finances from both sides–fewer people paying taxes and more people drawing on pensions and healthcare. Policy debates often focus on one fix at a time, such as raising taxes, reforming pensions, or boosting productivity.

pmc-11645474.title: Exome Sequencing Identified Susceptible Genes for High Residual Risks in Early‐Onset Coronary Atherosclerotic Disease
pmc-11645474.creator: Runda Wu, Ya Su, Jianquan Liao, Juan Shen, Yuanji Ma, Wei Gao, Zheng Dong, Yuxiang Dai, Kang Yao, Junbo Ge

pmc-12431667.title: The immune receptor SLAMF5 regulates myeloid-cell mediated neuroinflammation in multiple sclerosis
pmc-12431667.creator: Laura Bellassen, Keren David, Bar Lampert, Avital Sarusi-Portuguez, Michael Tsoory, Jazz Lubliner, Eran Hornstein, Michael Osherov, Ron Milo, Ori Brenner, Shirly Becker-Herman, Idit Shachar, Melissa Vazquez Hernandez, Melissa Vazquez Hernandez, Melissa Vazquez Hernandez, Melissa Vazquez Hernandez
pmc-12431667.description: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by demyelination of the central nervous system (CNS), leading to a broad spectrum of physical and cognitive impairments. Myeloid cells within the CNS, including microglia and border-associated macrophages, play a central role in the neuroinflammatory processes associated with MS.

pmc-12621431.title: Differences in Severity and Prognosis Between Bicuspid and Tricuspid Severe Aortic Stenosis
pmc-12621431.creator: Taiji Okada, Takeshi Kitai, Takeshi Morimoto, Chisato Miyakoshi, Tomohiko Taniguchi, Mitsuhiko Ota, Takao Kato, Kenji Ando, Nobuhisa Ohno, Norio Kanamori, Koichiro Murata, Yuichi Kawase, Tatsuhiko Komiya, Makoto Miyake, Yoshio Arai, Chisato Izumi, Tadaaki Koyama, Yutaka Furukawa, Takeshi Kimura
pmc-12621431.description: BackgroundBicuspid aortic valve (BAV) often leads to aortic stenosis (AS). However, current severity assessment and treatment strategies do not differentiate between BAV and tricuspid aortic valve (TAV) patients.ObjectivesThe purpose of this study was to investigate differences in echocardiographic indices used to evaluate disease severity and to compare long-term outcomes between BAV and TAV.
